Let's Look At ... FlavourArt JOY

It’s easy to get hyped up when you’re involved in communities that want to fan the flames. It’s not just here, it’s in video games, recreational firearms, knife collectors - you name it, there’s an online community hyping something as being the next “big” thing. The next game changer. The next staple that everyone is going to benchmark from here on out.

One of the worst things about hype, of course, is that there is a moderate-to-good chance that the product simply will not live up to the excitement that immediately surrounds it.

Which brings me to type up a few words about FlavourArt JOY, the “new kid on the block” hotness that’s sweeping through DIY communities internet-wide. Touted as a “bakery-style, funnel-cake inspired sweet blend” that’ll make one remember the simple joys of walking through a, say, county fair or carnival and enjoying all the lovely tastes and smells that surround you.

And much like county fairs and carnivals, the expectation and excitement over the prospect of attending is often a lot more fun and exciting than the fair itself.

I’m not immune to community excitement, so when word of JOY being back in stock at Bull City Vapor, I jumped at the chance to snag up a bottle of it and see what everyone was clamoring about.

Let’s sum it up in one, simple, Simpsons-esque word: meh.

First and foremost on the chopping block, as I’ve run it through subtanks and drippers alike - Joy gunks my coils up. Straight coils, twisted 28, pre-fab coil heads, doesn’t matter - give it a few hours of cycling through and steadily vaping and my coils get more junk on them than my arteries do after shovelling funnel cakes down my eager maw for an afternoon. I’m not a fan of the burnt junk off of coils, but when the coils are gunking over as quickly as it did with straight 4% JOY, having wattage a little too high makes them attempt to burn the gunk off, which in turn stains the entire rest of the tank with a twinge of “burnt.”

Imagine you’re stirring a big pot of chili. You leave the room to fiddle with coils or juice or whatever, and when you come back to the stove you realize you’ve left it on a little too long. Doesn’t matter that you’ve only burnt a tiny amount that was making direct contact with the bottom of the pot - all of the chili will taste burnt and carbon-y. Kinda like that.

I don’t demand that a flavoring be immune to coil gunking, as there are some wonderful flavorings out there that do it a lot faster than this. However, in the world of mixing our own juice, I have a hard time defending a flavoring that is prone to easily messing up coils.

Next up, I’m left wondering exactly what kind of flavoring this is supposed to be. Straight, at as high up as 7%, it just doesn’t have very much of a taste to it. It’s sweet on my lips and moustache after vaping, I can get a good mouth-feel and kind of a creamy, bakery-style sensation when vaping it, but it doesn’t pop out as any kind of discernible flavor in and of itself that I can find.

I honestly thought this was because I first jumped into a tank system with it (the excitement made me skip the dripper test as I usually do with new flavors and mixes). So, to the ol’ single coil Magma I go with it - and still, nothing much to write home about. If the sensations and taste-effects of it matched with a nice, full-bodied candy-bakery style taste, I’d have no complaints. It might not be my cup of tea, but for the life of me, I can sit there and chief down on it until it burns dry and not get so much as a smidge of actual flavor out of it. Candy-sweet moustache, but that’s about it.

Taking this in stride, I figure that this might be telling of it being a supplemental, or additive style flavoring. Looking around on my many various spots online, one simple recipe called for the addition of FA Cookie in a small amount (1%). With this mix, fresh, I still get nothing except the same - perhaps a slightly more full mouth-feel. Upping the Cookie to 3% makes it taste, more or less, like Cookie. That burns easily.

Given a few days to steep, nothing changed that stood out to me. Anything I attempted to throw at JOY, be it FA Forest Fruits, tobacco bases like FA Desert Ship or FA Cowboy Blend, nuts like CAP Pecan or TFA Black Walnut, even the highly esteemed FA Coconut - everything after adding JOY to it felt better in the vapor, but had muted taste with nothing substantial added.

At this point, I’m inclined to simply shrug and put it in the ol’ tacklebox for experimentation later.

But that’s where I’m having trouble with it the most - finding it’s place.

If I want the bready substance and aftertaste of baked goods, I can go with FA Cookie, or simple acetyl pyrazine, or even CAP Frosted Donut will do the trick. If it’s sweetness that I’m after, I’ve got a myriad of this cream and that, all of which would do the trick of sweetening up a juice mix a little. There’s no discernible taste to JOY for me, which makes it really difficult to place it in mixes.

At this point, I’m willing to even suggest just going full-bore with ethyl maltol (8% or more) to get the cotton-candy sweetness and mouth-feel without actual flavor adding to the mix.

As someone vested in the hobby, I’d have to give FA JOY a big ol’ fatty PASS at this point. Now, who knows? I’ve got 30ml of Joy and Cookie (3% and 1% respectively) steeping in a side drawer, that’ll get cracked open in a couple weeks. I’ve got 15ml of Joy and Coconut with Vienna Cream (all FA) sitting right next to it. Even an experiment with Joy, Desert Ship Flavorah Cured Tobacco and acetyl pyrazine, giving everything the good, long natural steep. I’m trying folks, I’m trying really hard to find the shimmer in the muck.

It just might turn around, given enough time, and lend a hand to the be-all end-all to delicious juice mixes.

...but I have my doubts. As far as I’m concerned, the hype train ran me over.

Again. Looking at you, SOHO.

tl;dr - I taste nothing, it gunks up my coils faster than it needs to, doesn't live up to the hype surrounding it. Mutes complimentary flavors. State Fairs aren't nearly as much fun as the prospect of attending. There are better additives to give you the same effects, don't beat yourself up over trying to get a bottle of it.

edited: Wrong tobacco in my 'experiment' bottle listed up above, it's Flavorah's Cured Tobacco, not Desert Ship. I tested it with Desert Ship, but that little (7ml) bottle has been chucked.
